newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude called slightly up tracking ACCESS.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude called slightly up tracking ACCESS.

text.p: NYMEX crude was called slightly higher Monday tracking ACCESS though traders said oil prices could trade near unchanged most of the day with little news and trading on London's IPE closed due to a U.K. holiday.
"I think we are going to rely mostly on technicals today because there is no news. We are drifting higher, but we could easily drift lower too," said a New York crude trader.
Crude was called unchanged to five cents a barrel higher and refined products were called flat to 0.25 cent a gallon higher.
On Friday, June crude ended 31 cents a barrel lower at $19.60. June heating oil settled down 1.31 cents a gallon at 53.02 cents while June gasoline finished 2.11 cents lower at $60.52 a gallon.
Dealers said the U.K. holiday may discourage speculators here from participating unless the thin trade results in exaggerated price action.

"After last week's action, we seem to be in a range between $19.40 and $20.40 (in crude). Even though London is closed, people on both sides of the Atlantic may have to get involved if it goes below $19.40," said a New York trader.
Despite Friday's losses, dealers noted both spot crude and heating oil were able to hold trendline support.

On Friday, prompt heat fell as low as 52.70 cents, slightly breaching a two-year trendline that extends from the March 15, 1995 low of 44.05 through the June 7, 1996 low of 49.20 on the daily spot continuation chart. June heat closed above the trendline and maintained it, but heating oil is seasonally out of favor.
June crude held a trendline extending from the double bottom of $18.96 on April 10 through the low April 17 of $19.10 on the daily spot chart.
